content:
After a lengthy developer and public beta period, Apple has officially released macOS 26.6 to all users with compatible Macs. Here's what's included in this update.

macOS 26.6 Officially Released

macOS 26.6 is now available, fixing over 150 security vulnerabilities, along with other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include an issue that incorrectly displayed deactivation notifications for some Intel-only apps, as well as bugs affecting HealthKit and Messages HDR screenshot functionality.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, macOS 26.6 may begin an indexing process to support the new Siri AI, Siri apps, and other features related to the next generation of Apple Intelligence.

Apple has so far only confirmed this approach for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but the Mac appears likely to follow the same approach. As users running the macOS 27 beta know, the indexing process takes several days, so starting early can reduce wait time after upgrading later this year.

The official version of macOS 26.6 is build 25G72, which differs from last week's release candidate (25G70).

Have you discovered any new features in macOS 26.6? Let us know in the comments.
